name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+25 PVI) after redistricting
Haynes' large fundraising advantage over Jackson
No polling or expert ratings, so forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The post-redistricting fundamentals give Democrats a margin of roughly 35 points, and Haynes has outraised Jackson by more than 20-to-1 with outside support on top. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, so the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing a competitive race, or major outside spending for Jackson, would be the first sign the safe rating needs revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat after redistricting redrew the Dallas-area district to be solidly Democratic, with a partisan lean of about 25 points toward Democrats. Frederick Haynes III, the Democratic nominee, has raised over $420,000 and holds roughly $120,000 on hand, supplemented by about $200,000 in outside support. Republican Everett Jackson has raised under $18,000 with about $1,200 remaining.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the lopsided money gap, and prediction markets, which price a Democratic win at roughly 95 percent. All available evidence points to the seat remaining safely in Democratic hands.
